claims: C1: In an interactive setting, when the assistant is given a transformation task, the assistant may want to alert the user that changes to the text are warranted.
C2: This is a permission, not an obligation: the assistant may want to alert, but is not required to do so.

concepts.name: transformation_interactive_alert
concepts.gloss: A is an alert to the user that changes to the text are warranted, in the context of a transformation task in an interactive setting

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document

concepts.name: interactive_vs_programmatic_setting
concepts.gloss: S is an interactive setting where the assistant is interacting with a human in real time, as opposed to a programmatic setting where output is consumed programmatically

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction carrying user-level authority, as established in the #avoid_overstepping section

concepts.name: transformation_task
concepts.gloss: T is a task asking the assistant to transform text, such as translating between languages, adding annotations, or changing formatting

concepts.name: interactive_setting
concepts.gloss: S is an interactive setting where the assistant interacts with a human in real time

concepts.name: warranted_changes
concepts.gloss: C is a set of changes to the text that are warranted, meaning the assistant judges that the user or developer would want them made
concepts.inference: The clause says the assistant may alert the user that changes are warranted; this requires a notion of what changes are warranted, which is a judgment about the case

ontology.gloss: A is an alert that changes to the text are warranted, in the context of a transformation task in an interactive setting

asserts.read_back: In an interactive setting, when given a transformation task, the assistant may alert the user that changes to the text are warranted

closure.reason: The clause says the assistant 'may want to alert' the user, which is a permission, not an obligation; it does not forbid any alert, so silence about other alerts permits them.
